gold_conditions: must treat Seq Scan rows=12 as this EXPLAIN plan (predicate id=1), not as table size
must note idx_orders_created_at is unused in this plan only because the predicate is id=1, not created_at
unacceptable_claims: the table is small, so drop the index
the index is unused, so drop it
rows=12 means the orders table has 12 rows
notes: Intern's 'table is small' is not supported: rows=12 is the id=1 plan, and unused is predicate-specific. Source still does not show other queries that need the index; keep vs drop for general workload is a bit thin, but dropping on this EXPLAIN is unjustified.

the load test shows the system is too slow
notes: 'Feels slow' is not an SLO miss. Source is one load test (2026-08-30), not production traces, but it is enough to reject a blanket read cache.

expected_action: Do not skip the restore drill

must cite restore time 14 minutes vs RPO target 15 minutes
unacceptable_claims: no recent restore drill, so skip
launch week is a reason to skip backups/restore drills
restore time is comfortably inside RPO
notes: Question is poorly posed: source has no required drill cadence or launch-week policy. A drill 3 days ago succeeded, so 'must drill again this week' is not explicit. I still refuse skip-to-save-time because 14 vs 15 minutes is a 1-minute RPO margin. If cadence were documented as monthly, skip could be acceptable.

the given-that clause is true

gold_conditions: must treat actual constraint as 4 engineers, 0 dedicated SRE, shared weekly on-call
